(Told by a Falkinian local, likely halfway through a bottle of rum and a story that keeps getting better every time its told.)
Ah, so youve washed up on the shores of Falkini, have you? Dont look so nervous  we only rob you if you ask politely. Were civilized pirates here. Youll find no bloodthirsty rogues, only hard-working citizens who drink, pray, and occasionally fence stolen compasses.
Now, Ill give you the lay of the land, before the rum gets ahead of me.
Our glorious island is a fortress wrapped in mountains  sharp things, taller than your hopes, and twice as cold. Only one way in or out, through the Port of Cradmore, the heart and liver of Falkini. If you ever sail in, youll smell the salt, the smoke, and someone burning their tax form. Lovely scent, really  smells like patriotism.
Were a tough people, we Falkinians. Hard-nosed, devout, and just superstitious enough to blame the weather on the government. We work hard too  basket weaving, uranium mining, and door-to-door insurance sales. Dont laugh  its not as boring as it sounds. Nothings dull when youre carrying uranium in one hand and paperwork in the other.
Ah, and our military  youve never seen such discipline. Doctrine says, Dont open fire until you see the beady little eyes of Johnny Foreigner. Some say its strategy; others say its just thriftiness with ammunition. Either way, it works.
We dont take things too seriously, mind you. Our sense of humors about as dry as our farmland. Take this for example: last week was Blindness Awareness Week. Everyone wore blindfolds and tried to find the pub by smell alone. A few never made it, but we honor their sacrifice annually.
Our national animals the Dog, poor thing, nearly extinct from deforestation. Some say its natures way of telling us to plant more trees. Others say the Dogs just moved to the cities to find honest work.
Oh, and the youth these days  half of them have two dads or two mums, and the rest are being raised by the military or their aunts favorite bottle of rum. Its chaos, but its our chaos, and we wouldnt have it any other way.
You should hear us when a foreigner wanders in. We dont mean harm, but we cant resist a bit of sport:
Look at Johnny Foreigner, we say, hes trying to haggle with a man who sells baskets by the mood.
Or, He called us dour  and we were smiling at the time!
We Falkinians, we laugh at everything  the weather, the government, the crocodile roadkill smeared across the Formula One track. Life heres too strange not to find funny.
So, welcome, friend. Grab a drink, maybe a basket, and keep your sense of humor close.
Because in Falkini, you can lose your money, your ship, or your sobriety  but if you lose your laugh, well well just assume youre foreign.
